paper_title: Token-Level Uncertainty Estimation for Large Language Model Reasoning
caption: Left: Uncertainty estimations in different token decoding temperature . Right: Influence of token decoding temperature on uncertainty-based AUROC scores.
model_annotation: The left plot illustrates the relationship between decoding temperature and uncertainty estimation for three regions—AU (Australia), TU (Turkey), and EU (European Union)—as measured by a token-level uncertainty estimation method. The x-axis represents the decoding temperature, ranging from 0.0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2, while the y-axis shows the uncertainty score, scaled from 0.000 to 0.175. The red line with circular markers, labeled AU, starts at approximately 0.125 when the decoding temperature is 0.0 and increases steadily to about 0.180 at a temperature of 0.8. The blue line with circular markers, labeled TU, begins slightly above 0.125 and follows a similar upward trend, reaching approximately 0.180 at a decoding temperature of 0.8. The green line with circular markers, labeled EU, remains nearly flat across all temperatures, staying close to 0.000, indicating minimal change in uncertainty estimation for the EU region regardless of the decoding temperature. This suggests that the uncertainty estimation for AU and TU is sensitive to changes in decoding temperature, whereas the EU shows little to no sensitivity.
